title: Introduce domain events with @nestjs/event-emitter to decouple modules and clean layering
description:
Goal
Adopt in-process domain events using @nestjs/event-emitter to decouple business logic from persistence (repositories) and remove cross-module layering smells. Services emit events when business state changes; listeners in other modules react (e.g., update statistics, enqueue messages) without repositories invoking higher-level services.

Motivation
- Eliminate repository -> service dependencies (e.g., profiles repo -> statistics service)
- Reduce circular DI and module coupling
- Make side-effects explicit, testable, and extensible

Scope (Phase 1)
- Add EventEmitterModule.forRoot() at app bootstrap
- Define event name constants and payload types per domain
- Update service layers to emit events (move side-effects out of repositories)
- Implement listeners in consumer modules
- Update/add tests (unit + integration where relevant)

Target modules and initial events/listeners
- User Profiles (emit):
  - user.profile.created { userId, createdAt, timezone }
  - user.profile.onboarding.updated { userId, stage, updatedAt, completedAt? }
  - user.profile.deleted { userId }
  - user.profile.simulation.updated { userId, simulation: Partial<...>, updatedAt }
  Consumers: Statistics (funnel steps)

- Statistics (listen):
  - On profile created/updated events, set funnel steps via StatisticsUserService
  - On WhatsApp and Journals/Audio events (below), increment counters

- WhatsApp (emit):
  - whatsapp.outbox.enqueued { outboxId, userId, phoneE164, bodyText, template? }
  - whatsapp.outbox.delivered { outboxId, deliveredAt, providerMessageId }
  - whatsapp.outbox.failed { outboxId, error }
  - whatsapp.inbox.received { id, fromWaid, type, text?, button?, userId?, contextMessageId? }
  - whatsapp.session.inbound.touched { userId, phoneE164, atIso }
  Consumers: Statistics (WhatsApp counters); Conversations (optional, to create messages from inbound)

- Conversations (emit):
  - conversations.message.created { messageId, userId, type, createdAt }
  - conversations.message.assistant.duplicateFlagged { messageId, userId, duplicateOfId }
  Consumers: Statistics (per-message metrics)

- Journals (emit):
  - journals.entry.created { userId, journalId, createdAt }
  Consumers: Statistics (journal counts)

- Audio Recordings (emit):
  - audio.recording.started/completed/canceled { userId, id, createdAt, durationSeconds? }
  Consumers: Statistics (voice metrics)

- Check-Ins (emit):
  - checkins.scheduled { userId, scheduleAt }
  - checkins.sent.whatsapp { userId, outboxId }
  Consumers: WhatsApp (enqueue), future analytics

- Goals (emit):
  - goals.macro.created/updated { userId, goalId }
  - goals.micro.created/updated { userId, goalId }
  Consumers: Agent/analytics (future)

- Activity (optional refactor):
  - Interceptor emits activity.api.logged; ActivityService listens and persists

Design constraints
- No new DB tables/queues; in-memory emitter only
- Repositories remain persistence-only; side-effects move to services/listeners
- Backwards compatible behavior for stats updates

Acceptance criteria
- App uses EventEmitterModule globally
- User profiles no longer call statistics from repository; stats updated via listener
- WhatsApp delivered/failed and inbox received events are emitted; statistics listener updates counters
- Tests cover emitters and listeners for Profiles, WhatsApp, and Statistics
- No module/provider circular dependency remains due to repositories

Non-goals (this story)
- Replacing cron-based orchestrators
- Introducing an external message bus

Follow-ups (Phase 2)
- Conversations granular stats processing via events
- Optional Activity interceptor refactor
- Broader adoption across Check-Ins, Goals if needed

features.title: App/Core - enable EventEmitter globally and define shared event types
features.description:
Add @nestjs/event-emitter as a dependency and register EventEmitterModule.forRoot() in AppModule. Create src/events with:
- events.constants.ts: string constants for event names (grouped by domain)
- events.types.ts: TypeScript payload interfaces per event
Provide a small helper for safe emit (guard undefined payload). Acceptance: App boots with emitter; basic smoke test emits and listens.

features.title: User Profiles - emit lifecycle events; remove repository side effects
Statistics - add listeners for profile/WhatsApp/journals/audio events
features.description:
Create listeners in statistics module to update funnels and counters:
- On 'user.profile.created' => setFunnelStep(OnboardingStart)
- On 'user.profile.onboarding.updated' => derive steps and setFunnelStepsCompleted
- On 'whatsapp.outbox.delivered' => incrementWhatsappDelivered
- On 'whatsapp.outbox.failed' => incrementWhatsappFailed
- On 'journals.entry.created' => incrementJournalsStarted/Completed
- On 'audio.recording.started/completed/canceled' => increment voice metrics and duration
Add focused unit tests for listeners. Ensure module wiring does not introduce DI cycles.

features.title: WhatsApp - emit outbox/inbox/session events and integrate with worker
Conversations - emit message lifecycle events; prepare stats hooks
Journals - emit entry created events
features.description: From JournalsService after successful create, emit 'journals.entry.created' { userId, journalId, createdAt }. Add unit tests verifying emission and payload shape.

features.title: Audio Recordings - emit started/completed/canceled events
Check-Ins - emit scheduler and send events
Goals - emit macro/micro goal lifecycle events
Activity (optional) - interceptor emits; service listens to persist
features.description: Refactor logging to events: LoggingInterceptor emits 'activity.api.logged' with request/response snapshot; ActivityService becomes a listener persisting via repositories. Maintain existing controller endpoints. Add tests verifying listener persistence and that interceptor never blocks responses.
